title: TS SDK: TypeBridge generator and streaming-shape hints for resilient discriminated output
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem statement: Developers using the TypeScript SDK rely on generated types and runtime validators to consume 'structured' LLM output. In streaming scenarios or with partial/ambiguous discriminator tags, current runtime guards either fail early (dropping streams) or accept too-liberal shapes (silently degrading correctness). We need a generator and runtime helpers that: 1) produce ergonomically typed discriminated unions for strict compile-time checks, 2) emit lightweight Zod + JSON-Schema artifacts for runtime validation and migrations, and 3) provide streaming-friendly progressive-parse helpers and shape-hints that tolerate partial chunks while enabling retries or multi-pass resolution.
acceptance_criteria: TypeBridge generator produces: discriminated union types, tagged variants, and an optional 'ShapeHint' interface for each model output schema
Generated artifacts include a Zod schema and JSON-Schema for each output type; these can be imported independently (no runtime coupling required)

Streaming helper (progressiveParse) accepts incremental chunks and returns: partialTokenCursor, best-effort typedCandidate(s), and a resolution API to finalize union membership when more tokens arrive
Runtime validators expose a 'softValidate' path (warnings + partial shape) and a 'strictValidate' path (throws/returns failure) configurable per-route
End-to-end tests cover: full-stream parse, mid-stream discriminator resolution, rewind+reparse with retries, and backward-compat with existing ts-sdk consumers
Docs and code examples added to SDK repo & Console docs showing migration from current zod helpers to TypeBridge
notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to generator + runtime helpers; separate follow-ups will add CLI integration and monorepo publish automation. We will favor non-breaking exports and maintain existing helper names where possible (deprecated shims provided).
implementation_plan: (1) Design TypeBridge IR: minimal metadata (tagKey, tagValues, shapeHint fields, stableFingerprint). (2) Implement generator that reads shape manifest (JSON-Schema) -> emits .d.ts types + Zod factory + JSON-Schema artifact. (3) Add streaming progressiveParse helper: incremental framing + lightweight shape-hint accumulation. (4) Add 'resolveUnion' strategy implementations (first-tag, probabilistic, deferred) and a feature flag to control default behavior. (5) Integrate runtime soft/strict validation APIs into existing client response processing pipeline. (6) Add unit/integration tests & example app. (7) Rollout plan: alpha feature flag on dev org -> staged rollout -> deprecate old helpers after 2 cycles.
tradeoffs:
- Strict immediate validation improves safety but can break streaming UX for large responses. We choose to default to 'softValidate' in streaming paths and 'strictValidate' in non-streaming/blocked routes.
- Emitting both Zod and JSON-Schema increases artifact size but greatly improves downstream interoperability (console dashboards, eval tooling). We'll provide a toggle to emit only one format for constrained bundles.
- Multi-pass resolution adds complexity to the SDK consumer API. To reduce cognitive load, default high-level helpers will return a Promise-like 'StreamCandidate' object with clear methods (await finalize(), onPartial(callback)).
implementation_notes:
- Generator input: canonical JSON-Schema registry (monorepo /schemas/ts-sdk). Use stableFingerprint (sha1) for cache keys and to attach to streaming prefix tokens.
- Streaming-shape hint: prefix token pattern e.g. 'SHAPE:{version}:{fingerprint}:{meta}' inserted by server or runtime when possible. SDK progressive parser will extract these hints early to short-circuit union resolution.
- Zod factories emitted as 'zodFromSchema' wrappers with opt-in coercion disabled by default. Provide small runtime helpers to do 'partialParse' that returns {status: 'partial'|'ok'|'invalid', data, diagnostics}.
- Retry behavior: when strictValidate fails after stream completes, client can call SDK.retryParseWithMode('lenient'|'probabilistic') which will re-run progressive parsing with different resolve strategies using historical tokens cached by the parser.
tasks: Implement generator prototype (node script) and add as pnpm workspace package
Write Zod factory templates and JSON-Schema emission in generator
Implement progressiveParse streaming helper in client runtime
Add resolveUnion strategies and feature flag wiring
Add full unit & e2e tests (jest + small integration harness with local runner)
Create migration examples and Console docs (how to import runtime validators)
Code review + security review (if required) + rollout
risks: Server does not always emit shape-hint prefixes; heuristics must be robust for missing metadata
Complexity of multi-pass parsers could mask bugs; strong tests required
Generated artifacts could increase package size for browser consumers; need opt-out and tree-shaking friendly exports

2025-02-28 - Design feedback (Marco Ruiz): examples should include common patterns: function-calling outputs, choices arrays, and nested discriminators. We should add a 'prettyFail' formatter for developer debugging.

2025-03-02 - Eng review (Rina Patel): suggested change: default to softValidate for streams, but allow per-route override via client config. Also requested additional tests around concurrent streams and memory retention of partial tokens.
